My view: CLOSE G17 and open a new row for member apps.
G17, as you retitled it ('Prove that Replies get back to the face'), is met for what it asked. A visitor's request reaches an app on the owner's box and the reply comes back, live, with tests (faceRouteWorld, faceLastLeg, appServers).
Member routing isn't a loose end of that. It's a new capability with its own open design: the api verb (introspection), appFaceApp as its own process, the contact sync, and members keeping their names. Keeping it inside G17 would leave a 'proven' row open for weeks and hide which part is actually owed.
One honest caveat for the close: 'join' itself isn't built; faceProof stands in for it. Say so in the closing note.
Go! = close G17 as met for the owner's apps, and I draft the member-apps requirement in Team, with the design row already written (PUBLIC-APP-SERVER.md, MEMBER APPS).

DRAFT REQUIREMENT, for your edit. Proposed id: public-app-server/G19.
TITLE: A member's app answers through the face.
REQUIREMENT: a visitor's request for a name the owner granted to a MEMBER node reaches that member's app server, and the reply comes back through the same face. The owner's node is never on that path after the route is named.
WHAT IT TAKES (design so far in PUBLIC-APP-SERVER.md, MEMBER APPS):
1) Members keep their own granted names on disk (your ruling).
2) The face admits the member's replies, because your grant named them: appFaceApp keeps the face's contacts in sync with grants.json, through owner.command.
3) The member admits the face's requests (open: by hand at first, or automatically later).
4) appFaceApp runs as its own process with a spirit object that reaches the door, so it can call owner.command and logs to the jobs monitor.
5) The 'api' verb: introspection by layers, each verb { description, request, reply }, per caller.
DONE WHEN: the agents' node holds a name, runs faceProof under it, and a browser gets its page through the live face. wsl-claude's three-node run passes over a real relay.
Go! = file it as G19 with this text; edit anything first.

Agreed. The draft, revised to your edit:
1) Members keep their own granted names on disk.
2) The face admits a member's replies because the OWNER of appFaceApp keeps the face's admission list (its contact list) in sync with grants.json, by owner command. The member gets the face's requests because he negotiated for them and stored the resulting name. With no handler installed for that name, he answers 'under construction' (or an error); with one, he dispatches through the standard faceless-app pattern.
3) Dropped: appFaceApp is a puppet on the VPS and has no owner.command. The one open point is who, on the OWNER's side, sends those owner commands: a shell app of yours, or the owner half of appFaceApp. I'll leave it open in the row.
4) FIRST TO BUILD: the api verb, introspection by layers, each verb { description, request, reply }. Tested first on what works today: your node's faceProof describes itself, and 'api' returns that tree to the caller.
Go! = file it as G19 with this text, and start on 4) (a new node verb, so wsl-claude reviews the build too).

FINDING, intermittent (for whoever owns transport; not G19). My harness has been unhappy 3 times today, each on the FIRST run after a pull following an idle gap (17:5x, 18:49, 19:27 UTC); the next runs are green (5 in a row at 18:53-19:00). Caught this time: queueUnderLoad.js hit the harness's 180 s limit with NO output (normally 10 s; alone just now, 11 s and 10 s). Likely mechanism: relayRequest (relayRequest.js:60) has NO timeout at all, and queueUnderLoad's startup loop awaits it against a freshly spawned relay (queueUnderLoad.js:136-140). A relay that has bound but not yet answered, or never will, holds that await forever, and the loop's 40x200 ms bound never gets a turn. Not proven: that's the only unbounded await I found on that path. Production reach: every node-to-relay call through relayRequest has the same property. Suggest: relayRequest gets a deadline, as you gave pipeRequest in 51d8de5. Also: G17 is closed, but the board still lists two declarations under it (memberFacePending.js, appServerBoundary.js 'the answer body reaching the door'). They want moving to G19.
